parsed.rationale: The structural evidence explicitly shows `shared_field_count: 0` and `jaccard: null`, meaning these two protocols share zero overlapping members. `HLSAVPlayerProtocol` (in `Shared/Playback/Sources/HLSPlayer/Protocol/HLSAVPlayerProtocol.swift`) exposes low-level AVFoundation primitives such as `currentTime:() -> CMTime`, `rate:Float`, and `seekableTimeRanges:[NSValue]`, while `TimeShiftablePlayer` (in `Shared/Playback/Sources/PlaybackCore/Protocols/TimeShiftablePlayer.swift`) exposes a higher-level, domain-specific surface including `isAtLiveEdge:Bool`, `secondsBehindLive:TimeInterval`, `eventStream:AsyncStream<AudioPlayerInternalEvent>`, and `stateStream:AsyncStream<PlayerState>`. The only superficial overlap is the bare `play:()` member, but the two protocols encode entirely different abstraction layers — one wraps an AV transport, the other models a time-shifting audio player — making any inheritance relationship semantically misleading rather than clarifying. Introducing a parent protocol with a single shared member would create a false coupling between unrelated domain concepts.
